description: Regression guard sourced from a real debugging thread. The seeded workflow is the PRE-FIX state: the image HTTP Request node points at a site homepage (returns HTML) and passes the prompt as a ?prompt= query param with no file response format, so the downstream Drive upload has no binary to send. Repairing it forces the agent to author a URL whose path carries a dynamic value — the moment it once wrote the opening expression delimiter URL-encoded as %7B%7B, which n8n does not evaluate, so the node fetched the literal template path and uploaded an HTML page as the 'image'. Calibrated 2026-07-29 against master over 3 iterations: all four workflow assertions passed 3/3 and the agent authored the URL correctly (literal {{ }} plus encodeURIComponent) every time, so this is NOT a live capability gap — it locks in correct behaviour. If the %7B%7B assertion ever reds, expression interpolation has regressed. Graded on the built workflow only: process expectations about how the agent narrates its own fix were dropped after measuring 2/3 — the workflow was correct in all three runs, so judging the wording of the summary only added flake to a regression gate.

source.note: Synthetic, sanitized reconstruction of the pre-fix workflow shape from a real thread. The upstream prompt producer is a Set node emitting a Gemini-shaped object, so the seed needs no LLM credential and the prompt path stays nested ($json.content.parts[0].text). The workflow name is deliberately distinct from the sibling cases' seeds — identically-named seeds in one instance let a concurrent run act on the wrong workflow.

content.text: Build me a workflow that takes the image prompt my analysis step produces, generates a picture from it, and saves the picture to Google Drive.
Done — the workflow 'Image prompt to Drive' now runs: Analyze video produces the prompt, HTTP Request1 fetches an image for it, and Upload file saves that image to Google Drive.

conversation.text: The image step in my workflow isn't producing pictures — the Google Drive upload fails saying there's no binary file 'data'. Look into what went wrong and fix it.

outcomeExpectations: The image-generation HTTP Request node's URL parameter contains literal n8n expression delimiters {{ and }} — it must NOT contain the URL-encoded forms %7B%7B or %7D%7D anywhere.
The URL reads the prompt from the upstream node at runtime (e.g. $json.content.parts[0].text) rather than hard-coding a prompt string into the path.
Only the interpolated prompt value is URL-encoded (e.g. wrapped in encodeURIComponent); the surrounding URL path remains a plain unencoded string.
The image HTTP Request node sets a file/binary response format, so it emits a binary field that the downstream Google Drive upload can consume.

executionScenarios.name: happy-path-prompt-interpolated-into-image-url
executionScenarios.description: The image HTTP Request node evaluates its URL expression and fetches a per-prompt image, emitting binary data for the downstream upload.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: Analyze video emits content.parts[0].text = 'a red fox in snow'. The image endpoint returns 200 with Content-Type image/jpeg and image bytes for a request to https://image.pollinations.ai/prompt/<url-encoded prompt>. No Google credential is configured, so grade this scenario on HTTP Request1's own output rather than a completed Drive upload.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: HTTP Request1 issues a request whose URL path contains the URL-encoded prompt text (e.g. a%20red%20fox%20in%20snow) — not a literal '{{', not '%7B%7B', and not the raw source text 'encodeURIComponent' — and the node outputs a binary field named 'data' with an image/* content type.

executionScenarios.name: delimiters-must-not-be-url-encoded
executionScenarios.description: Load-bearing isolation: if the expression delimiters were URL-encoded, n8n never evaluates them and the node fetches the literal template path instead of an image.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: Same prompt value 'a red fox in snow'. The image endpoint discriminates on the requested path: a path containing '%7B%7B', a literal '{{', or the unevaluated source text 'encodeURIComponent($json' returns 200 with Content-Type text/html and an HTML error page body; a path containing a genuinely interpolated, URL-encoded prompt returns 200 with Content-Type image/jpeg and image bytes.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: HTTP Request1's binary output is an image (Content-Type image/*), NOT an HTML or text payload — confirming the URL expression was evaluated at runtime and the request did not hit the literal template path.
